honesty_notes: This is the OLDEST dated source in the entire shard — over 5 years old at capture time, and predates any of the current pricing figures registered here (EV-04 through EV-08). Explicitly flag its age; do not present the 'really cheap' characterization as describing 2026 pricing without this caveat.
The 150-minutes-in-a-day figure is a single anecdote from one reviewer under an unknown, likely-since-changed plan — never generalize this into a stated Murf throughput capability.

entries.claim: A disclosed-methodology, affiliate-monetized hands-on test (mrreviewai.com, published 2026-05-30, updated 2026-06-27) documents a live-account free-plan test: the reviewer confirms the 10-minute generation cap is a one-time lifetime allocation with no reset, confirms the no-download restriction via a screenshotted export-dialog quote, and separately ran identical scripts through Murf and ElevenLabs, scoring Murf 4.3/5 overall (calling its 'emotion system... its biggest advantage') versus ElevenLabs at 4.8/5 on the same naturalness comparison — a third, independently-sourced data point (after Visme and the Capterra sample) suggesting a real, if narrow, realism gap versus ElevenLabs specifically.
entries.quote: The 10 minutes is a one-time lifetime allocation. It does not reset. Once you use it, you're done with the free tier... Unlock unlimited downloads — You are on free plan. Upgrade to one of the paid plans to export your projects... Murf's emotion system is its biggest advantage.
entries.platform: mrreviewai.com (disclosed-methodology hands-on test with an explicit affiliate-link disclosure — self-interested; published 2026-05-30, updated 2026-06-27, captured 2026-08-08)
entries.label: independent-test

coding.aspect: free-plan mechanics independently confirmed via live account; head-to-head naturalness score vs. ElevenLabs on identical scripts

honesty_notes: Carries an explicit affiliate disclosure ('This article contains affiliate links. If you purchase through our Murf AI link, we may earn a small commission') — self-interested despite the disclosed, specific, reproducible methodology (live account, timestamped remaining-minutes figure, direct screenshot quote). Label accordingly wherever cited.

The 4.3 vs. 4.8 star comparison is this single reviewer's own subjective scoring scale, not a blind test or a defined-sample count — present as one dated reviewer's head-to-head impression, not as an objective naturalness measurement, and do not average or combine it numerically with Murf's own benchmark (EV-12) or the Capterra star ratings.

entries.claim: A second disclosed-methodology, affiliate-monetized hands-on test (fahimai.com, published 2026-02-14) reports an 8-project, 90-day, 4-language test (5 client training videos + 3 explainer videos), paid for by the author on their own credit card, contacting support 3 times. The reviewer describes Murf's voices as 'natural, not robotic' — a data point in TENSION with EV-13/EV-03/EV-16 above — and reports cutting per-voiceover production time from '3-5 hours to 20 minutes,' concluding the Creator plan ('$19/month') 'pays for itself after two or three projects' compared to hiring a human voice actor.
entries.quote: The voices sound natural. Not robotic... Time per voiceover [reduced from] 3-5 hours [to] 20 minutes... pays for itself after two or three projects.
entries.platform: fahimai.com (disclosed-methodology hands-on test with explicit affiliate links; published 2026-02-14, captured 2026-08-08)

coding.aspect: ease-of-use time-savings and value-for-money claim, plus a positive (not-robotic) voice-quality impression that contrasts with other sources
coding.plan_tier_if_stated: Creator $19/month (as third-party stated by this source, matching EV-07/EV-08)

honesty_notes: RELIABILITY CAVEAT: the same publisher's WellSaid Labs article was independently flagged in the wellsaid-labs-review shard for an internal date self-contradiction ('90-vs-60-day'). This specific Murf article shows no equivalent contradiction on inspection this run, but the general reliability concern for this domain is carried forward — use this source's SPECIFIC, checkable claims (time-per-voiceover, cost comparison) rather than its overall narrative framing.

Deliberately does NOT include the article's headline '99.38% pronunciation accuracy' claim — see EV-12's honesty_notes for why this specific figure was excluded from quoting (it does not match the vendor's own current benchmark page's stated range and recurs as an apparently uncredited copied number across multiple third-party sites).
Carries an explicit affiliate disclosure ('reader-supported... potential affiliate commissions') and multiple in-article affiliate CTAs — self-interested despite the disclosed methodology.

entries.claim: hackceleration.com (a commercial AI-agency site with its own tool-implementation COI) compiled 15 reviews from G2, Trustpilot, and TrustRadius and relays 3 individually dated, named quotes: Ishan S. (2026-06-04) notes occasional pronunciation issues with health-related terminology; Pooja K. (2026-01-29) reports voices 'sometimes... sound robotic and not natural' alongside a customer-support complaint; Tiara D. (2026-04-07) calls the Studio interface 'a total nightmare to navigate' with lag/glitching during editing. These quotes could NOT be independently re-verified at their origin platforms this run — G2 and Trustpilot were both blocked (HTTP 403) for direct fetch, as in every prior Mimo shard — so this entry is a SECONDARY, relayed source, not a primary one.
entries.quote: Sometimes I notice the voices sound robotic and not natural... The actual Studio interface is a total nightmare to navigate... the whole thing kept lagging.
entries.platform: hackceleration.com (commercial AI-agency site compiling G2/Trustpilot/TrustRadius reviews it did not itself host originally — relayed secondary source, agency has its own tool-implementation COI; page captured 2026-08-08, individual relayed quotes dated Jan-Jun 2026)

coding.aspect: relayed, defined-sample (of 15 G2/Trustpilot/TrustRadius reviews compiled Jan-Jun 2026) negative/mixed data points on pronunciation, voice naturalness, support, and Studio interface stability

honesty_notes: FLAGGED for resolver: a coder could argue for exclusion entirely on chain-of-custody grounds — this curator fetched hackceleration.com's page live this run (satisfying protocol §4's re-fetch requirement for THAT URL), but cannot independently confirm these three quotes appear verbatim on G2/Trustpilot/TrustRadius, since those platforms are themselves blocked. Present explicitly as 'relayed via hackceleration.com,' never as if directly sourced from G2/Trustpilot.

This is a defined sample WITH a denominator (n=15 reviews, Jan-Jun 2026 date window per hackceleration's own disclosure) — usable per MEP §6's honest-ceiling reporting rules, but only 3 of the 15 are individually quoted/named here; do not imply the other 12 support the same specific complaints without their own quotes.

The Tiara D. Studio-interface-lag complaint is the ONLY negative ease-of-use data point in this entire shard beyond the generally positive Capterra/vendor framing — genuinely useful for an honest easeOfUse sub-score, but resting on a single relayed, unverified-at-source quote; weight accordingly.
